A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TTRV. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original recognition and VQA experiments, reward ablations, cross-dataset evaluations, latency measurements, and repeated-run results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds reward-ablation results and evaluations on three additional VLM backbones.

M1.justification: The frequency reward, entropy reward, combined objective, and GRPO update remain unchanged in Equations 1–9. The pseudocode in v1 Appendix E and v2 Section 10 is also unchanged apart from formatting.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight recognition and eight VQA datasets, including the same cross-dataset transfer scenarios. The expanded ablations and additional backbones use retained datasets; CAPTURe already used free-form answers in v1.

E2.justification: New Table 13 adds unadapted MM-Eureka-7B, ThinkLite-VL-7B, and VisionReasoner-7B as baselines for paired comparisons with TTRV. The new TENT discussion identifies the existing no-frequency-reward ablation as a surrogate; it does not establish a separately added TENT implementation.

E3.justification: Table 13 extends evaluation to three additional 7B model configurations. Existing splits, image filtering, adaptation sample budgets, rollout settings, and greedy-decoding evaluation remain unchanged between v1 Appendix A and v2 Section 6.

E4.justification: Table 3 extends the reward-component and majority-voting ablations from MathVista, SEED, and AI2D to MathVerse and CRPE. Section 9.4 and Table 13 extend the model-portability analysis. Existing sampling, random-reward, single-example, latency, and cross-dataset analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 1 retains its five-run variance reporting, Table 11 retains the same five-run results, and Table 10 retains its mean-and-standard-deviation reporting. No new seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are provided for the added results.

E6.justification: v2 adds MathVerse and CRPE ablation entries and paired results for three additional models, with Table 13 reporting gains of 0.07–2.02 percentage points. For example, MM-Eureka-7B scores 78.92 without TTRV and 80.94 with TTRV on MathVista. Table 10 adds percentage overheads derived from unchanged timings. Previously reported benchmark scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and optimization equations are unchanged. Neither version supplies a theoretical explanation or proof for the claimed recovery of latent capabilities; v2 retains this limitation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unsupervised test-time RL, complementary rewards, performance gains, data efficiency, and applicability across models. The added experiments support existing contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: Sections 2 and 4.3 newly interpret the entropy-only ablation as a TENT surrogate and explain obstacles to directly applying normalization-based and class-entropy TTT methods to decoder VLMs. The latent-capability interpretation and stated lack of theoretical explanation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The optimizer, learning rate, reward weight, token limits, hardware, vLLM usage, prompts, and pseudocode are retained. Both versions give the same project-page link and statements about the review code ZIP, execution instructions, and public release upon acceptance.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Norm, TENT, and the three additional model studies, and expands discussion of prior TTT methods' applicability. It removes the Snell et al. test-time-scaling citation and associated comparison. The broader positioning against TTRL and supervised RL remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the section sequence are retained. Changes include a localized rewrite of the TTT discussion, a CAPTURe explanatory footnote, removal of the Einstein quotation, supplementary-material cross-reference edits, and renumbering Appendices A–E as Sections 6–10.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column presentation, substantially reflowing text, equations, references, prompts, and tables. Figure 1 moves above the abstract, and retained figures and tables are resized or regrouped. Table 3 gains two columns, Table 10 gains a percentage column, and Table 13 is added.

improvement.justification: Expanded reward ablations in Table 3 and evaluations on three additional backbones in Table 13 modestly strengthen the existing reward-design and portability claims. The improvement is limited: the new model gains lack uncertainty estimates, and the retained inconsistency between the main text's 20-sample description and Table 9's 500-sample InternVL3-8B results remains unresolved.
